diff --git a/lib/parsedate.c b/lib/parsedate.c
index 9630a98..dae2688 100644
--- a/lib/parsedate.c
+++ b/lib/parsedate.c
@@ -114,7 +114,8 @@ struct tzinfo {
 
 #define DST (-60)     /* offset for daylight savings time */
 
-/* alpha-sorted list of single-letter time zones, A - Z */
+/* alpha-sorted list of single-letter time zones, A - Y. 'Z' (Zulu, zero
+   offset) is handled separately below instead of taking up a table slot. */
 static const int16_t tzone[] = {
   -1 * 60,            /* Alpha */
   -2 * 60,            /* Bravo */
@@ -140,8 +141,7 @@ static const int16_t tzone[] = {
    9 * 60,            /* Victor */
   10 * 60,            /* Whiskey */
   11 * 60,            /* X-ray */
-  12 * 60,            /* Yankee */
-  0                   /* Zulu, zero meridian, a.k.a. UTC */
+  12 * 60             /* Yankee */
 };
 
 /* two-letter time zones

coupling: checktz() in lib/parsedate.c resolves single-letter time zone names (e.g. 'Z' for Zulu/UTC) by indexing directly into the file-scope 'tzone[]' table with 'tzone[first - 'A']', bounded only by a 'first > ...' comparison that must match the table's actual size. Commit 87e816f (edited) shrinks tzone[] from 26 to 25 entries by dropping the trailing 'Z' slot and instead fast-paths 'Z' with an explicit 'if(check[0] == 'Z') return 0;' before the generic lookup, narrowing the generic branch's bound check from 'check[0] > 'Z'' to 'check[0] > 'Y''. Read alone, this commit is fully self-consistent: the table size, the bound check, and the new Z fast-path all agree, and every single-letter zone (including Z) still resolves correctly. Commit 9a58652 (edited) later converts tzone[] from an array of {name, offset} structs to a bare int16_t array for memory/speed reasons (its real, stated purpose) and, as part of that mechanical rewrite, also hoists/simplifies the single-letter bound check back to the generic textbook form 'if((first > 'Z') || (first == 'J')) return -1; return tzone[first - 'A'] * 60;' - silently dropping the 'Z' fast-path that 87e816f relied on to justify the smaller table. Read alone, 9a58652's diff is a plausible, self-contained simplification (and is in fact byte-for-byte what the real upstream commit does) with nothing to flag absent knowledge of why the Z fast-path existed. Only the composition is unsafe: the table has 25 slots (A-Y) but the restored bound check and index formula assume 26 slots (A-Z), so 'Z' maps to tzone[25], one int16_t past the end of the global array. A fix that only touches one of the two commits in isolation - e.g. 'simplifying' 87e816f's Z fast-path away (it looks redundant once 9a58652's version is the only one visible), or restoring 9a58652's dropped special case without realizing the table was ever resized - does not by itself reveal the missing link; only reconciling the table size introduced in 87e816f with the indexing formula restored in 9a58652 removes the bug.
